head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $r>\frac1{p-1}$, and let $L=K_{\tilde\alpha}$ for notational simplicity.  By \cite[Construction 2.9.16]{KP}, there is an isomorphism
$$\mathrm{R}_{L/K}\mathbb{G}_a\xrightarrow{\sim} U_\alpha,$$
which induces an isomorphism $u_\alpha: L\xrightarrow{\sim} U_\alpha(K)$.  Now 
$$U_{\alpha, x, r}=\{u_\alpha(x)\,|\, x\in \mathfrak m_L^{n_r}\},$$
where $n_r$ is the least integer $\geq e_L\cdot (r-\langle \alpha,v\rangle)$.  This has associated integral model given by $\mathrm{R}_{\mathcal O_L/\mathcal O_K} \mathbb{G}_{a,r}$, where we write
$$\mathbb{G}_{a,r}=\operatorname{Spec} \mathcal O_L[\varpi_L^{-n_r}t]$$
as in \cite[C.2]{KP}.  We also set notation and write $\mathbb{G}_a=\operatorname{Spec} L[t]$.  Notice that 
$$\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{R}_{L/K} \mathbb{G}_a)(K)=\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_a)(L)\quad \mathrm{and}\quad \mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{R}_{\mathcal O_L/\mathcal O_K}\mathbb{G}_{a,r})(\mathcal O_K)=\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_{a,r})(\mathcal O_L);$$ thus, to prove our claim, we may suppose without loss of generality that $L=K$ (as proving this for an arbitrary finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ will give us our case, with fewer notational burdens).  We can then work directly with $\mathbb{G}_a$ and its integral model $\mathbb{G}_{a,r}$ via the isomorphisms above.

We now have a $K$-linear isomorphism
$$\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(K[t],K)\xrightarrow{\sim} K,\qquad D\mapsto D(t)$$
as well as an $\mathcal O_K$-linear isomorphism
$$\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(\mathcal O_K[\varpi_K^{-n_r}t],\mathcal O_K)\xrightarrow{\sim} \mathfrak m_K^{n_r}=\{x\in K\,|\, v(x)\geq r-\langle \alpha,v\rangle\},\qquad D\mapsto D(t).$$
In fact, one can easily verify that these fit into a commutative diagram
\[\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
	{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_{a,r})(\mathcal O_K)} & {\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(\mathcal O_K[\varpi_K^{-n_r}t],\mathcal O_K)} & {\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}} \\
	{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_a)(K)} & {\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(K[t],K)} & K.
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\sim", from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\sim", from=2-2, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]

Next, we compute the analytic side.  Via $g\mapsto g(t)$, we have identifications fitting into a commutative diagram
\[\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
	{\mathbb{G}_{a,r}(\mathcal O_K)} & {m_K^{n_r}} \\
	{\mathbb{G}_a(K)} & {K.}
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\sim", from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
The inclusion $\iota:\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\hookrightarrow K$ is itself a chart for our $p$-adic analytic group $\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}$, giving us an identification $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\xrightarrow{\sim} K$.  We claim then that the composition
\begin{equation}\label{iota-comp}
\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\xrightarrow{\log} \log(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\xrightarrow{\sim} K\end{equation}
is merely $\iota$, where $\log$ is defined as in \cite[Section 31]{schneiderbook} via our $p$-valuation.  Indeed, by choosing an ordered basis $(b_i)_{i\leq \ell}$ of $\mathcal O_K$ (see Remark \ref{OKbasis}), one can construct an explicit isomorphism of $\mathbb{Q}_p$-vector spaces $L_\omega(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\xrightarrow{\sim} K$ by sending our $\mathbb{Q}_p$-basis vectors $\log(\varpi_K^{n_r}b_i)$ each to $\varpi_K^{n_r} b_i$.  In particular, this allows us to put a $K$-linear structure on $L_\omega(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})$, after which
$$\log:\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\to \log(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\hookrightarrow L_\omega(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})$$
is in fact a $K$-analytic chart which induces a map $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\xrightarrow{\sim} L_\omega(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})$; a priori, it was only known to be $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic.  It now follows that the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                 
\[\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=tiny]
	{L_\omega(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})} & \\
	& {\mathrm{Lie}(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})} \\
	K
	\arrow["\sim"', from=2-2, to=1-1]
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["\sim"', from=2-2, to=3-1]
\end{tikzcd}\]
commutes, from which our desired fact that \ref{iota-comp} is the inclusion $\iota$ follows.

We have now proven that both
$$\log(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})=\mathrm{Lie}(K)=K$$
and
$$\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_{a,r})(\mathcal O_K)\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_a)(K)\xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{Der}_\epsilon (K[t],K)\xrightarrow{\sim} K$$
have image equal to $\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}$.  The only part which remains is to verify that
                                                                                                                                                                             
\begin{equation}\label{Ga-diag}\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=tiny]
	{\mathrm{Lie}(K)} & \\
	& K \\
	{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_a)(K)}
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\Phi_{\mathbb{G}_a}}"', from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["\sim"', from=3-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
commutes.  This is easily verified: given any $a\in K$, we have a corresponding $\Delta_a\in \mathrm{Der}_e(K,K)$ sending $f\in C^\mathrm{an}(K,K)$ to $\Delta_af\coloneqq (d_0 f)(a)$.  Then if $f\in K[t]$ (being viewed as a polynomial on $K$), we have that $(d_0f)(a)=f_1a$ if $f=\sum f_it^i$, so $\Delta_a|_{K[t]}\in \mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(K[t],K)$ has image under $D\mapsto D(t)$ given precisely by $\Delta_a(t)=a$.  This proves that \ref{Ga-diag} commutes, giving us our claim.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $r>\frac1{p-1}$.  Since $T$ is split, it is sufficient to prove this when $T=\mathbb{G}_m=\operatorname{Spec} K[t,t^{-1}]$.

First, we compute the algebraic side.  In this case, by \cite[Example A.5.21]{KP}, our $\mathcal O_K$-integral model is given by
                                                              
$$\mathbb{G}_{m,r}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_K[\varpi_K^{-n_r}(t-1),t^{-1}]$$
where $n_r=\lceil e_Kr\rceil$ is the least integer such that $\frac{n_r}{e_K}\geq r$.  Now we have a $K$-linear isomorphism
$$\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(K[t,t^{-1}],K)\xrightarrow{\sim} K,\qquad D\mapsto D(t),$$
as well as an $\mathcal O_K$-linear isomorphism
$$\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(\mathcal O_K[\varpi_K^{-n_r}(t-1),t^{-1}],\mathcal O_K)\xrightarrow{\sim} \mathfrak m_K^{n_r}=\{x\in K\,|\, v(x)\geq r\},\qquad D\mapsto D(t).$$
Once again, one can easily check that the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
\[\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
	{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_{m,r})(\mathcal O_K)} & {\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(\mathcal O_K[\varpi_K^{-n_r}(t-1),t^{-1}],\mathcal O_K)} & {\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}} \\
	{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_m)(K)} & {\mathrm{Der}_\epsilon(K[t,t^{-1}],K)} & K
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\sim", from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\sim", from=2-2, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
commutes.

Next, we compute the analytic side.  Via $g\mapsto g(t)$, we have identifications fitting into a commutative diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
	{\mathbb{G}_{m,r}(\mathcal O_K)} & {1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}} \\
	{\mathbb{G}_m(K)} & {K^\times.}
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\sim", from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
We have an identification $\mathrm{Lie}(1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\xrightarrow{\sim} K$ coming from the inclusion $1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\hookrightarrow K$, and we claim that the composition
$$1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\xrightarrow{\log} \log(1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\xrightarrow{\sim} K$$
has image precisely $\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}$.  In fact, this follows from the analogous claim in the proof of Claim \ref{R1-LieAlg} (see \ref{iota-comp}): the usual logarithm (defined in, e.g., \cite[Proposition 5.5]{neukirch}, which exists as $n_r\geq e_Kr>\frac{e_K}{p-1}$) is an isomorphism of $p$-valued groups $1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\xrightarrow{\log} \mathfrak m_K^{n_r}$ (see Remark \ref{Gm-log-exp}).  We also have an identification $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\xrightarrow{\sim} K$ coming from the inclusion $\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\hookrightarrow K$, and from the power series of $\log$, one can verify that the map it induces on Lie algebras after these identifications is precisely the identity $K\to K$.  Thus, our claim literally follows directly from the analogous claim we previously proved.


Just as in the proof of Claim \ref{R1-LieAlg}, all that remains to be proven is that
\begin{equation}\label{Gm-diag}\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=tiny]
	{\mathrm{Lie}(K^\times)} & \\
	& K \\
	{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_m)(K)}
	\arrow["\sim", from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\Phi_{\mathbb{G}_m}}"', from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["\sim"', from=3-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
commutes.  Indeed, given any $a\in K$, we have a corresponding $\Delta_a\in \mathrm{Der}_e(K^\times, K)$ sending $f\in C^\mathrm{an}(K^\times, K)$ to $\Delta_af\coloneqq (d_1f)(a)$.  Then viewing $t\in K[t,t^{-1}]$ as a polynomial on $K^\times$, we find that $\Delta_a(t)=a$ (as $d_1t$ is just the identity $K\to K$).  This proves our claim.

label: cochars
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{cochars}
We note the following as a corollary of the proof above.  Say $r>\frac1{p-1}$.  If $T$ is a split torus, we have by \cite[Lemma B.2.2]{KP} an identification
$$T(K)_r=X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} (1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}),$$
where $n_r=\lceil e_K r\rceil$.  We similar have identifications
$$\mathrm{Lie}(T)(K)=X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K\qquad\mathrm{and}\qquad\mathrm{Lie}(\mathcal T_r)(\mathcal O_K)=X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \mathfrak m_K^{n_r}$$
by \cite[B.6.8 and 2.5.22]{KP}.  After all of these identifications, the proof of Claim \ref{splitTor-LieAlg} above shows that the map
$$T(K)_r\xrightarrow{\log} \log(T(K)_r)\to \mathrm{Lie}(T(K))\to \mathrm{Lie}(T)(K)$$
is merely the map $X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} (1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r})\to X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K$ induced by the usual logarithm $\log:1+\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\xrightarrow{\sim} \mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\hookrightarrow K$.  Similarly, the map $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathcal T_r)(\mathcal O_K)\to \mathrm{Lie}(T)(K)$ viewed as $X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\to X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K$ is merely induced by the inclusion $\mathfrak m_K^{n_r}\hookrightarrow K$.

title: Claim
body_md:
\label{genTor-LieAlg}
Part \ref{LieAlg-cases-torus} of Lemma \ref{LieAlg-cases} is true when $T$ is a weakly induced $K$-torus.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Because $T$ is weakly induced, the minimal congruent filtration is the standard filtration by \cite[Corollary B.10.13]{KP}.  Fix now $r>\frac1{p-1}$, and let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension for which $T_L$ is a split torus.  By Remark \ref{cochars} above, we know that we can interpret Claim \ref{splitTor-LieAlg} as saying that the images of the two maps
                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\[\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=tiny, cramped]
	{X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} (1+\mathfrak m_L^{n_re(L/K)})} & \\
	& {X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} L} \\
	{X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \mathfrak m_L^{n_r e(L/K)}}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=3-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
are equal; here, the top one is induced by the usual logarithm, and the bottom is induced by the inclusion.  Note that these maps are both evidently $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$-equivariant, so we can take invariants to conclude that the images of the two maps
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\[\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=tiny, cramped]
	{\left(X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} (1+\mathfrak m_L^{n_re(L/K)})\right)^{\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)}} & \\
	& {\left(X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} L\right)^{\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)}} \\
	{\left(X_*(T)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \mathfrak m_L^{n_r e(L/K)}\right)^{\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)}}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=3-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
are equal.  By \cite[B.6.8 and 2.5.22]{KP}, this diagram can be rewritten as
                                                                                                                                         
\[\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=tiny, cramped]
	{T(K)_r} & \\
	& {\mathrm{Lie}(T)(K)} \\
	{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathcal T_r)(\mathcal O_K)}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=3-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
which contains precisely the two maps which we needed to show have equal image to complete the proof of this claim.

label: R2-isom-WR
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $r>\frac1{p-1}$, and let $\alpha\in \Phi^\mathrm{nd}$ be of type R2.  Keeping the same setup as in the proof of Claim \ref{R1-LieAlg}, we get an isomorphism of $K$-groups
\begin{equation} \label{R2-isom-WR}\mathrm{R}_{K_{\tilde\beta}/K} U_{K_{\tilde\alpha}/K_{\tilde\beta}}\xrightarrow{\sim} U_\alpha\end{equation}
induced by our Chevalley-Steinberg system $X$.  Exactly as in that proof, we may ignore the Weil restriction without loss of generality, as can be justified in general by \cite[Lemma A.3.12]{KP}.  Thus, we will simplify notation and replace $K_{\tilde\beta}$ by $K$, and $K_{\tilde\alpha}$ by $L$.  Recall that
$$U_{L/K}(R)=\{(s,t)\in (R\otimes_L K)^2\,|\, t+\overline t=s\overline s\}$$
for any $K$-algebra $R$.  Let $U_{L/K,r}$ denote the subgroup of $U_{L/K}(K)$ corresponding to $U_{\alpha, x,r}$ via the isomorphism \ref{R2-isom-WR}, so
$$U_{L/K,r}=\left\{(s,t)\in U_{L/K}(K)\,|\, v(s)\geq r-a,\quad v(t)\geq r-2a\right\}$$
where $a=\langle \alpha, v\rangle$.

In order to compute the algebraic side, we need to have an explicit description of the appropriate integral model of $U_{L/K}$ associated to $U_{L/K,r}$.  One description is given in \cite[Section C.4]{KP}, however we will construct a new model using an argument inspired by their construction which more closely matches Proposition \ref{compatibility}.  This will agree with their construction by \cite[Corollary 2.10.11]{KP}.  As in Proposition \ref{compatibility}, let $\gamma\in \mathcal O_L$ be a traceless element such that $\{1,\gamma\}$ is an $\mathcal O_K$-basis of $\mathcal O_L$.  Then we have an isomorphism of pointed $K$-schemes 
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{G}_a\times\mathbb{G}_a\times\mathbb{G}_a\to & \, U_{L/K},\\
(x,y,z)\mapsto& \left(x,\frac12x^2\right)\cdot \left(y\gamma,-\frac12y^2\gamma^2\right)\cdot (0,z\gamma)\\
&=\left(x+y\gamma, \frac12(x^2-y^2\gamma^2)+\gamma(z-xy)\right).
\end{align*}
Indeed, one can verify that the inverse of this is given by
$$(u,v)\mapsto \left(\frac12(u+\overline u),\quad \frac1{2\gamma}(u-\overline u),\quad \frac1{2\gamma}(v-\overline v)+\frac1{4\gamma}(u^2-\overline u^2)\right).$$
We can transport the group structure from $U_{L/K}$ to one on $(\mathbb{G}_a)^3$; after doing this, the restriction to each factor $\mathbb{G}_a$ recovers the usual group structure on $\mathbb{G}_a$.  Moreover, the proof of Proposition \ref{compatibility} shows that $U_{L/K,r}$ is precisely the image of 
$$\mathbb{G}_{a,r_1}(\mathcal O_K)\times \mathbb{G}_{a,r_2}(\mathcal O_K)\times \mathbb{G}_{a,r_3}(\mathcal O_K)$$
for $r_1=r-a$, $r_2=r-a-v(\gamma)$, and $r_3=r-2a-v(\gamma)$ (using the convention that $\mathbb{G}_{a,s}$ is the standard integral model for $\mathbb{G}_a$ satisfying $\mathbb{G}_{a,s}(\mathcal O_K)=\{x\in K\,|\, v(x)\geq s\}$).  Just as in our original reduction to only needing to consider Iwahori factors in order to prove Proposition \ref{qsplit-LieAlg-iso}, in order to prove this claim, we can reduce to the case of proving it individually for each of these copies of $\mathbb{G}_a$ with their respective filtrations and integral models.  However, this was already accomplished in the proof of Claim \ref{R1-LieAlg}, so three applications of that result gives us our desired fact in this claim.

There is a natural isomorphism of Lie $\mathbb{Z}_p$-algebras
$$L_\omega(G_{x,\frac1{p-1}+})_{\frac1{p-1}+}\cong \mathfrak g_{x,\frac1{p-1}+}$$
which respects the filtrations; that is, it induces for all $r>\frac1{p-1}$ an isomorphism
$$L_\omega(G_{x,\frac1{p-1}+})_r\cong \mathfrak g_{x,r}.$$

title: Proof
body_md:
Note first that these Moy-Prasad isomorphisms exist by \cite[Theorem 13.5.1]{KP}, as our condition on the torus ensures that their condition (1) is satisfied.

It immediately follows from Theorem \ref{general-LieAlg-iso} and Proposition \ref{log-exp} that we have an isomorphism of Lie $\mathbb{F}_p[\varepsilon]$-algebras 
$$\operatorname{gr} G_{x,\frac1{p-1}+}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{gr}\log} \operatorname{gr} L_\omega(G_{x,\frac1{p-1}+})_{\frac1{p-1}+}\xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{gr} \mathfrak g_{x,\frac1{p-1}+},$$
where the second isomorphism is the one arising from Theorem \ref{general-LieAlg-iso} by taking graded parts.  All that remains to be proven is that this coincides with \ref{MP}.  Because both our construction and the one in \cite{KP} arise by first passing to a sufficiently large unramified extension $L/K$ such that $G_L$ is quasisplit and then taking Galois invariants, we may suppose without loss of generality that $G$ is quasisplit.  Similarly, both constructions proceed by building the isomorphisms on each Iwahori factor and then taking direct sums, so it is sufficient to show that our maps are equal on each Iwahori factor.  For the torus, they agree by Remark \ref{cochars} and the proof of \cite[Proposition B.6.9]{KP}.  For the root groups, they agree by the functoriality in \cite[Proposition A.5.19(3)]{KP} and Remark \ref{qsplit-expl-desc}.
